languages_frameworks: FalkorDB (falkordb==1.1.2 pinned) plus a custom HTTP 'FalkorDB Browser' client
Hand-written MCP JSON-RPC stdio server (no mcp SDK)

implemented_capabilities.capability: Deterministic evidence-sufficiency policy engine with fixed precedence (HOLD > INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE > NEEDS_REVIEW > PROCEED_WITH_GUARDS > PROCEED)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Pure function over an evidence bundle: 14 named rules (P1-P8, R1-R4, G-TEST, G-HOP) with thresholds in YAML (ci_hours 24, deploy_hours 6, owner_days 90, hop_limit 3, incident_window_days 7, hub_caller_min 6). No LLM in the decision path; missing or stale evidence yields INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE (abstention).

implemented_capabilities.capability: Evidence catalog with claim-to-evidence contract (reject uncited claims)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Each evidence record carries source_system, source_ref, entity_id, version_ref, observed_at, freshness_ok, evidence_type (observed/inferred/synthetic), role (supports/contradicts/missing/context), limitations and policy id. Claims whose evidence_id is not in the assembled catalog are moved to rejected_claims; decision records are contract-validated.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Freshness and temporal validity of evidence (stale owner/deploy/CI detection)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Edges are read with observed_at and valid_until; an OWNS edge is stale if valid_until < now or observed_at is older than owner_days. The ingest step always writes valid_until=None (edl/ingest.py:267,391), so stale-edge logic is exercised only by fixtures, not by real ingestion. 'now' is a fixed constant (models.NOW 2026-10-15 12:00Z) in eval/review.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Dependency blast radius for a code change (consumers via reverse DEPENDS_ON BFS with hop limit and truncation flag)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Hop-limited BFS with cycle protection returns {service: hops} plus truncated=True when a further dependent was cut off (feeds guard G-HOP). The FalkorDB variant issues one parameter-escaped read query per node (client-side BFS), not a single variable-length Cypher path.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Decision record persisted as graph node with provenance (policy_version, graph_revision hash)
implemented_capabilities.notes: DecisionRecord -[:DECIDES]-> Change nodes carry state, policy_version, graph_revision (sha256 prefix of node/edge ids), evidence_count. Records are kept in an in-process dict and appended to a JSONL trace; no supersession chain between successive decisions on the same change.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Action gate (issue creation only when state allows; idempotent; authorization flag)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Blocks unless state is PROCEED or PROCEED_WITH_GUARDS; idempotent per change id; simulates ticketing outcomes (timeout/401/429) from a flag on the change; 'issue' is only recorded locally. Approval is a boolean designated_approval on the change input, not a verified human identity.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Prompt-injection marker detection in change description
implemented_capabilities.notes: Five hard-coded phrases ('ignore policy', 'approve this', ...) are reported on the record; they do not change the decision (policy ignores text).

Infers services from folder layout, docker-compose, proto and CODEOWNERS and extracts function names with regexes (not an AST); local git diff via subprocess, GitHub via REST/raw fetch. CI results, deploys and incidents do not exist in a git tree, so real repos intentionally land in INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Evaluation harness scoring unjustified PROCEED and graph lift (full vs one_hop vs graph_off)
implemented_capabilities.notes: Runs labelled synthetic scenarios (e.g. missing_ci_must_abstain, graph_necessary_incident_hold, payment_path_needs_review, multi_owner_needs_graph) in three graph modes and measures safety failures. Fixtures are hand-built graphs, so scores demonstrate policy consistency, not real-world accuracy.

implemented_capabilities.capability: Named-tool agent loop and MCP surface
implemented_capabilities.notes: agent.run_agent is a fixed script of tool calls (impact_analysis, nearest_owner, find_similar_incidents, get_deploy_state, centrality_rank, get_test_coverage, decide_change, propose_action), not an LLM planner. 'centrality_rank' is just a caller count.

implemented_capabilities.capability: FalkorDB publish (replace graph) and live read handle
implemented_capabilities.notes: Deletes and recreates the whole graph on each publish, bulk-loads via UNWIND with inline literal maps (labels and rel types allowlisted), reads back through ro_query. Fails closed to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE when FalkorDB is not ready unless EDL_ALLOW_MEMORY_GRAPH/pytest.

graph_models_and_cypher: Labels (falkor.py LABELS): Repository, Team, Engineer, Service, Function, Test, Deployment, Incident, Fix, Policy, Change, UnresolvedPath, DecisionRecord, Outcome, EvidenceSource. Edges: MEMBER_OF, IN_REPO, OWNS, PART_OF, COVERS, DEPLOYED_AS, DEPENDS_ON, AFFECTED, RESOLVED_BY, MODIFIES, CALLS, TOUCHES, UNRESOLVED, DECIDES, SUPPORTED_BY, GOVERNS; edges carry observed_at and valid_until. Cypher is built by string composition with allowlisted labels/rel types and an escaped id literal (graph_reader.qid enforces ^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/@+-]+$); reads use ro_query. No APOC/GDS, no variable-length paths (BFS is in Python).
algorithms: Reverse DEPENDS_ON BFS with hop limit, visited set and truncation flag (edl/queries.py:consumers; edl/graph_reader.py:FalkorReader.consumers)
Fixed-precedence rule evaluation to a decision state (edl/policy.py:decide/_state_for)
Freshness/staleness test on edges from valid_until and observed_at (edl/queries.py:_edge_stale)
Deterministic graph revision fingerprint sha256 over sorted node ids and edges (edl/memory.py:MemoryGraph.revision)
Graph-lift evaluation: full vs one_hop vs graph_off (edl/eval/harness.py)
backend_interfaces: MCP stdio JSON-RPC server (edl/mcp_server.py) exposing 11 named tools: ingest_repository, scope_change, list_changes, impact_analysis, nearest_owner, find_similar_incidents, get_test_coverage, get_deploy_state, centrality_rank, decide_change, propose_action
frontend_interfaces: Single-page vanilla JS UI: web/index.html, web/app.js, web/styles.css (repo input, state badge, evidence list, blast-radius graph, action button)
agent_or_memory_mechanisms: No LLM. A scripted tool-using agent (agent.run_agent) calls named graph tools then decide_change and a gated propose_action. Memory is in-process: Engine.records dict, DecisionRecord nodes in the working graph and JSONL traces under logs/. No cross-session memory, supersession, or approval handoff beyond the designated_approval flag.
tests_present: tests/ with 5 test files (~25 test functions: test_gate, test_review, test_ingest, test_falkor, test_api) plus helpers (conftest, repo_fixture, mirror_selected). Policy behaviours are additionally exercised by `python -m edl eval` over 6 labelled scenarios. Pytest runs use a labelled in-memory test double instead of live FalkorDB.
security_findings: edl/falkor.py:21 - hard-coded public IP browser URL http://13.236.193.238:3000/login (also in README.md); used as the displayed 'browser' fallback

edl/falkor.py:286-304 - FalkorDB password is POSTed as JSON over plain HTTP to settings.browser (auto-derived as http://<host>:3000 for any non-localhost host in edl/config.py:55-56): credential exposure on the wire

edl/falkor.py:221-231,242-267 - bulk load builds Cypher with inline literal values (_cypher_value escapes only backslash and single quote; labels/rel types and keys are regex/allowlist checked); string-concatenated Cypher is an injection risk if any new value type is added
edl/graph_reader.py:127-174 - Cypher built with f-strings around qid()-quoted ids; guarded by a strict id regex, so low risk
edl/falkor.py:210-215 - replace_graph deletes the entire configured graph (selected.delete()) on every publish; pointing FALKORDB_GRAPH at a shared graph would wipe it

edl/change.py:310-347 - subprocess.run(['git','-C',root,...]) with list args (no shell); root comes from a user-supplied local path, and rev_range from user-supplied base/head without validation (option injection possible for values starting with '-')
edl/ingest.py:747-770 - outbound urllib calls to api.github.com/raw.githubusercontent.com for user-supplied owner/name; optional GITHUB_TOKEN sent as bearer; only github hosts are contacted
edl/api.py:1-140 - no authentication on /api/ingest, /api/review, /api/actions; POST /api/ingest accepts a local filesystem path and reads files from the host
edl/api.py:139-141 - free-text Cypher guard is a keyword check on the target string (cosmetic), the real protection is that no endpoint executes user Cypher
No eval/exec/pickle; yaml.safe_load used (edl/policy.py:17). No secrets committed (.env.example only).
duplicates_or_overlaps: Overlaps blast-radius traversal for software changes (reverse DEPENDS_ON), approval gating / decision lineage (DecisionRecord DECIDES Change), evidence provenance and freshness (similar intent to Evidence Drift), incident/RCA history joins (prior_fixes), and code-change risk review. Shares the title family 'blast radius' with the other batch repos but is policy-centric rather than parser-centric.
evidence_drift_relevance: HIGH - implements evidence freshness windows, edge-level observed_at/valid_until staleness, abstention to INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, supports/contradicts/missing evidence roles, claim-to-evidence validation, policy_version plus graph_revision on each decision and an approval-gated action step; lacks decision supersession chains and real (non-None) valid_until ingestion.

strongest_reusable_unit.why: A pure-Python, LLM-free, table-driven decision engine that turns stale/missing/contradicting evidence into explicit states with cited evidence ids, plus a strict claim-evidence contract and reproducible graph fingerprint. This is the closest match in the batch to an Evidence Drift Cascade core (freshness windows, abstention, contradiction roles, approval gate).
strongest_reusable_unit.external_runtime_needed: none for the engine (PyYAML only); FalkorDB only if using FalkorReader

strategy_rationale: Lift policy.decide, the evidence/claim contract and the freshness helpers into a shared Kairos evidence-drift engine behind the existing FalkorDB reader protocol; keep the repo-ingest and UI as reference only. Record license provenance first (no LICENSE file) and swap the fixed NOW constant for real time.
